summary.name: ChessCafe
summary.one_liner: ChessCafe is a free desktop 3D chess game for Mac and Windows where pieces animate and fight during captures, with computer opponents, hot-seat play, and engine-vs-engine duels.
use_cases: Play chess against the computer at adjustable strength
Play a friend on one shared computer
Watch two chess engines play each other
Learn chess by seeing capture outcomes
Play chess offline without an account
summary.what_it_does: The app renders chess as an animated 3D battle: pieces turn toward their target, walk there, and strike, with armies and battlegrounds that can be chosen per side. It offers three computer opponent strengths (Squire, Knight, Warlord), with the engine running on its own thread. Hot-seat mode lets two people share one computer, with an optional camera swing. Standard rules are supported, including castling, en passant, promotion, optional clocks, take-backs, resign, board flip, and a move record copyable as PGN. It runs fully offline with no account, and graphics quality is auto-detected on first launch.
notable: Pieces animate and fight during captures instead of sliding
Works offline with no account; nothing is sent anywhere
Built on the open-source King's Gambit - Medieval 3D Chess project (MIT licence)
Engine-vs-engine duel mode with the interface hidden
caveats: Platforms are limited to Mac and Windows; no Linux or mobile version is mentioned
The page does not state whether the app itself is open source; only the underlying project is credited as MIT-licensed
